markets.trend: Late October was dominated by heavy, whipsawing foreign flows with institutions buying steadily throughout. Monday Nov 2 saw a sharp US-driven intraday selloff met by aggressive domestic institutional buying while both foreigners and individuals sold into the rebound. Tuesday Nov 3 flipped that pattern entirely: KOSPI fell -3.59% (its worst day in recent weeks) as BOTH foreign and domestic institutions turned net sellers (-₩1.5tn and -₩0.5tn respectively) while retail individuals bought the dip aggressively (+₩1.66tn).
markets.interpretation: The Nov 3 reversal is a caution flag: domestic institutions, the prior stabilizing bid, joined foreigners in selling into the selloff, leaving retail as the sole buyer of the dip -- a riskier configuration than Nov 2's setup, since retail-led dip-buying without institutional follow-through tends to be less durable support.
